entry.title: 🇯🇵 Presenting at IEEE FG 2026
entry.content:
I had the wonderful opportunity to present my PhD research at the Doctoral Consortium of the 20th IEEE International Conference on Automatic Face and Gesture Recognition (FG 2026), held in Japan.

The Doctoral Consortium is a dedicated session for PhD students to share their ongoing research, exchange ideas, and receive constructive feedback from senior researchers in the computer vision and pattern recognition community.

🎤 Presentation

I presented my PhD research on Multi-view Temporal Action Recognition in open-space and real-world environments. The work addresses a key challenge in the field: while most existing methods focus on action recognition in constrained, limited-space settings, real-world scenarios demand robust recognition across open and distributed environments with diverse sensor configurations.

The talk covered the motivation, problem formulation, and my current research directions — including multimodal and multi-view approaches for accurate action recognition using distributed sensors.

📄 Certificate of Attendance (PDF)

🤝 Engaging with the Community

The Doctoral Consortium brought together PhD students from diverse institutions, creating a rich environment for discussion and collaboration. Attendees engaged actively throughout the presentations, and the feedback I received from both peers and senior researchers was truly valuable for shaping the next steps of my research.

Gratitude

I am grateful to the FG 2026 organizers for creating a dedicated space for doctoral researchers, and to my advisors and collaborators at Nagoya University and RIKEN for their continued guidance and support.

Being part of this community continues to motivate my research, and I look forward to the conversations and collaborations that grow from events like this.

entry.title: 🇩🇪 Attending the Freiburg Rising Stars Conference

link.title: 🇩🇪 Attending the Freiburg Rising Stars Conference

entry.content:
I had the pleasure of attending the Freiburg Rising Stars Conference 2025/2026, hosted in Freiburg, Germany — a unique event bringing together outstanding early-career researchers from diverse disciplines. The conference provided an inspiring platform to exchange ideas, present research, and connect with peers and senior academics in a highly collaborative environment.

🌟 Highlights

Throughout the event, I had the opportunity to:

  • Engage in insightful discussions across interdisciplinary topics
  • Learn from keynote talks and panel sessions led by leading researchers
  • Present my work and receive valuable feedback
  • Connect with fellow rising researchers from around the world

🤝 Community & Connections

One of the most rewarding aspects of the conference was the people. From casual coffee break conversations to deeper academic exchanges, the event fostered a strong sense of community.

It was especially motivating to be surrounded by passionate researchers, each contributing unique perspectives and ideas.

I am truly grateful to the organizers for creating such a welcoming and stimulating environment. Events like this play an important role in shaping future collaborations and research directions.

Looking forward to staying in touch with the amazing people I met — and hopefully crossing paths again soon!

entry.title: 🇺🇸 Presenting at IEEE/CVF WACV 2026
entry.content:
I was excited to be back at IEEE/CVF WACV 2026 this year, held in Tucson, Arizona (March 6–10, 2026). After a great experience at WACV 2025, returning this year was especially meaningful — I presented 2 papers at the poster sessions:

  • ViCoKD: View-aware Cross-modal Distillation for Multi-view Action Recognition
  • PADM: A Physics-aware Diffusion Model for Attenuation Correction

🌃 Networking & Tucson Nights

WACV is always more than just paper presentations — it is also about building connections. I had a fantastic time catching up with old friends and meeting new colleagues. We enjoyed an evening together at a rooftop venue overlooking the beautiful Tucson cityscape.

Gratitude

I would like to express my sincere thanks to my co-authors and advisors for their continued support and collaboration. Presenting at WACV 2026 was a truly rewarding experience, and I look forward to building on the discussions and ideas that emerged from this conference.

See you at the next one!

entry.title: 🇯🇵 Attending ACM Asian School on HPC and AI 2026

link.title: 🇯🇵 Attending ACM Asian School on HPC and AI 2026

entry.content:
I had the incredible opportunity to attend the ACM Asian School on HPC and AI 2026. The program brought together students, researchers, and professionals from across Asia and beyond to explore the latest advances in High Performance Computing (HPC) and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

This experience was not only academically enriching but also culturally inspiring.

🗻 Visiting a World-Class Supercomputer Facility

One of the highlights of the school was visiting a state-of-the-art supercomputing Fugaku center. Seeing the computing racks in person made everything we learned feel tangible and real.

Standing next to the system reminded me that behind every large AI model and scientific simulation lies massive engineering effort and computational power. This visit deepened my appreciation for the infrastructure that powers modern AI research.

🗾 Cultural Exchange & Memories in Japan

Exploring the city together was another unforgettable part of the journey. Walking through vibrant streets at night, enjoying local food, and sharing laughter with new friends made the experience even more meaningful.

Science connects us globally, but shared experiences make those connections lasting.

📜 Certificate

I also received a Certificate of Completion from the ACM Second Asian School on High Performance Computing and Artificial Intelligence (2026). The certificate recognizes successful participation in the program and completion of the training activities on modern high-performance computing and AI systems.

entry.title: 🇯🇵 Attending SCA/HPCAsia 2026
entry.content:
I had the incredible opportunity to attend SCA/HPCAsia 2026 (Supercomputing Asia 2026), held in Osaka, Japan. The conference brought together researchers, engineers, and industry leaders working at the forefront of High-Performance Computing (HPC), AI, Cloud, and Quantum Computing.

This event was not only technically inspiring but also a valuable chance to connect with the global HPC community.

Quantum Computing: IBM Quantum System Two

Another impressive exhibit was the IBM Quantum System Two, showcasing the integration of quantum computing with HPC systems. The hybrid future of classical HPC and quantum computing is becoming increasingly tangible — and SCA 2026 made that vision feel closer than ever.

Networking & Community

Beyond the technical sessions, SCA provided a valuable space to connect with fellow researchers and industry professionals. Conversations ranged from GPU architectures to distributed training strategies and future collaborations.

Moments like these remind me that progress in computing is powered not only by machines — but by people.

entry.title: 🇲🇾 Best Oral Award at ACM Multimedia Asia 2025

link.title: 🇲🇾 Best Oral Award at ACM Multimedia Asia 2025

entry.content:
I am deeply honored to share that our paper received the Best Oral Award at the 7th International Conference on ACM Multimedia Asia 2025 (MMAsia 2025), held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

This recognition means a lot to our team and marks a memorable milestone in my research journey.

🏆 Best Oral Award

According to the official certificate, the award was presented for our paper:

“Q-Adapter: Visual Query Adapter for Extracting Textually-related Features in Video Captioning.”

Authors: Junan Chen, Trung Thanh Nguyen, Takahiro Komamizu, Ichiro Ide

Receiving this award during the conference was both surprising and incredibly motivating. It reflects not only the technical contribution of our work but also the clarity and impact of our presentation.

🎁 Conference Moments

MMAsia 2025 was more than just research sessions. It was also a wonderful opportunity to connect with fellow researchers, explore emerging ideas, and experience Malaysian hospitality. From the conference materials to cultural elements integrated into the event, everything reflected thoughtful organization and community spirit.

🌃 Exploring Kuala Lumpur

Beyond the conference venue, Kuala Lumpur offered beautiful city views and vibrant nightlife. Visiting the iconic Petronas Twin Towers was an unforgettable moment. Experiences like this remind me that academic journeys are not only about research achievements but also about cultural exchange and personal growth.

Gratitude

I would like to sincerely thank my co-authors and collaborators for their hard work and support. This award belongs to the entire team. Winning the Best Oral Award at ACM MMAsia 2025 motivates me to continue pursuing impactful research in multimodal learning and video understanding.

Looking forward to future conferences and collaborations!

entry.title: 🇹🇼 International Summer School 2025 at Academia Sinica

link.title: 🇹🇼 International Summer School 2025 at Academia Sinica

entry.content:
This summer, I had the wonderful opportunity to attend the International Summer School 2025 organized by the Institute of Mathematics, Academia Sinica, in Taipei, Taiwan.

The program took place from June 25 to July 16, 2025, and focused on:

Nonstationary Time Series Analysis for Biomedical Artificial Intelligence

It was an intensive and intellectually rewarding three-week experience that combined advanced mathematical theory with modern AI applications in biomedical research.

🎓 Certificate of Achievement

At the end of the program, I received a Certificate of Achievement from Academia Sinica, recognizing the successful completion of the course. This certification represents not only participation, but also deep engagement with advanced topics in mathematical modeling and biomedical AI.

🌆 Experiencing Taipei

Outside the classroom, Taipei offered a vibrant cultural experience. From exploring historic streets to enjoying local cuisine, the city provided a perfect backdrop for reflection and inspiration.

Moments like these remind me that academic journeys are not only about research progress, but also about cultural exchange and personal growth.

entry.title: 🇺🇸 Best Student Paper Award at IEEE FG 2025

link.title: 🇺🇸 Best Student Paper Award at IEEE FG 2025

entry.content:
I am deeply honored to share that our paper received the Best Student Paper Award at the IEEE International Conference on Automatic Face and Gesture Recognition (FG 2025).

This recognition is a significant milestone in my PhD journey and a proud moment for our entire research team.

🏆 Awarded Paper

The award was presented at FG 2025, held in Clearwater, Florida, USA. Our awarded paper is titled:

MultiSensor-Home: A Wide-area Multi-modal Multi-view Dataset for Action Recognition and Transformer-based Sensor Fusion

Authors: Trung Thanh Nguyen, Yasutomo Kawanishi, Vijay John, Takahiro Komamizu, and Ichiro Ide

Receiving this award among many strong international submissions was both surprising and incredibly motivating.

🌊 Conference Experience in Florida

FG 2025 was held in Clearwater, Florida — a beautiful coastal city.

🤝 Gratitude

I would like to sincerely thank my co-authors and mentors for their continuous guidance and support. This achievement would not have been possible without their collaboration and encouragement.

Winning the Best Student Paper Award at IEEE FG 2025 strengthens my motivation to continue pursuing impactful research.

entry.title: 🇺🇸 Presenting at IEEE/CVF WACV 2025
entry.content:
I had the incredible opportunity to present our latest research, “CT-to-PET Translation: A Large-scale Dataset and Domain-Knowledge-Guided Diffusion Approach”, at the IEEE/CVF WACV2025 conference. This experience was both an honor and an exciting moment to share our findings with the computer vision communities.

Our work was selected for an oral presentation, which allowed me to introduce our novel approach to a broad audience. I also participated in a poster session, engaging in discussions with researchers from diverse backgrounds. These interactions provided valuable insights and new perspectives on improving our methodology further.

Networking & Discussions: Conference is not just about research but also about making new connections.

WACV 2025 was an enriching experience, and I am excited to apply the feedback and ideas from discussions into future research. Stay tuned for upcoming publications and collaborations!

entry.title: 🇳🇿 Presenting at ACM Multimedia Asia 2024
entry.content:
I had the incredible opportunity to present my latest research at ACM Multimedia Asia 2024, held from December 3–6, 2024, in Auckland, New Zealand. The conference brought together researchers and practitioners from the multimedia community to share cutting-edge advancements and insights.

During the conference, I presented my paper titled “Action Selection Learning for Multi-label Multi-view Action Recognition”. My research focuses on enhancing action recognition models by leveraging multi-view perspectives and multi-label learning techniques to improve accuracy and robustness in real-world scenarios.

A huge thank you to my co-authors, advisors, and the conference organizers for making this event a success. I truly appreciate the opportunity to contribute to the multimedia research community.
